examples.question_text: Find the gradients of the tangents to $y = x^2 - 4x + 2$ at $x = 1$ and $x = 3$, then find their angles of inclination to the nearest minute.
Find, to the nearest minute, the angles of inclination of the tangents to $y = 9 - x^2$ at its $x$-intercepts.
examples.solution_text:
At the $x$-intercepts, $y = 0$.
$\begin{aligned}9 - x^2 &= 0 \\ x^2 &= 9 \\ x &= -3 \text{ or } x = 3\end{aligned}$

$f'(x) = -2x$

At $(-3,0)$:
$m = f'(-3) = 6$
$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta &= 6 \\ \theta &= \tan^{-1}(6) \\ &\approx 80.5377^{\circ} \\ &\approx 80^{\circ}32'\end{aligned}$

At $(3,0)$:
$m = f'(3) = -6$
$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta &= -6 \\ \theta &= 180^{\circ} + \tan^{-1}(-6) \\ &\approx 99.4623^{\circ} \\ &\approx 99^{\circ}28'\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Find any points on $y = \dfrac{x^3}{3} - 8$ where the tangent has an angle of inclination of $45^{\circ}$.
examples.solution_text:
$m = \tan 45^{\circ} = 1$

$f'(x) = x^2$
$\begin{aligned}x^2 &= 1 \\ x &= 1 \text{ or } x = -1\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}f(1) &= \dfrac{1}{3} - 8 \\ &= -\dfrac{23}{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}f(-1) &= -\dfrac{1}{3} - 8 \\ &= -\dfrac{25}{3}\end{aligned}$

The points are $\left(1,-\dfrac{23}{3}\right)$ and $\left(-1,-\dfrac{25}{3}\right)$.

examples.question_text: Find the point on $y = 4\sqrt{x}$ where the tangent has an angle of inclination of $60^{\circ}$.

Find the exact angle of inclination of the tangent to each curve at the given value of $x$.

(a) $y = x^2 - 7x + 2$ at $x = 3$.

(b) $y = \dfrac{1}{3}x\sqrt{x}$ at $x = 12$.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$f'(x) = 2x - 7$
$\begin{aligned}m &= f'(3) \\ &= 2(3) - 7 \\ &= -1\end{aligned}$

$\tan\theta = -1$

The angle of inclination is obtuse, so $\theta = 135^{\circ}$.

(b)
$y = \dfrac{1}{3}x^{\frac{3}{2}}$
$\begin{aligned}f'(x) &= \dfrac{1}{2}x^{\frac{1}{2}} \\ &= \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{2}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}m &= f'(12) \\ &= \dfrac{\sqrt{12}}{2} \\ &= \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$

$\tan\theta = \sqrt{3}$

The angle of inclination is acute, so $\theta = 60^{\circ}$.
